intro: Logistics managers coordinate people, freight and schedules, skills that general and operations management depend on. The closest of the 25 careers below is General and Operations Managers, with a 91% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $105,770, about 1% less than the $107,230 transportation and distribution managers earn.
why_it_works: Running a warehouse or fleet means planning capacity, solving delays and training crews under tight deadlines. O*NET rates coordination at 3.75 out of 5 for this job, and problem solving, instructing and systems analysis at 3.62. Operations, project and sales management use the same skills. Almost every match needs no new degree. The gaps are reading people and managing staff.
tips: Sales Managers earn $148,270, which is 38% more, and value supply chain knowledge in B2B sales.
Project Management Specialists are an 85% match if you want project-based work with fewer night calls.
Loss Prevention Managers are an 81% match, with a median of $141,900 for their broader group.

faq.q: What jobs can former logistics managers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are General and Operations Managers (91%), Logisticians (87%) and Project Management Specialists (85%), based on O*NET 31.0. Logisticians earn $82,320, which is 23% less than the $107,230 median for transportation, storage and distribution managers.

faq.q: Which careers for logistics managers pay more?
faq.a: 6 of the 25 matches pay more. Chief Executives earn $213,990 (100% more), Marketing Managers $166,790 (56% more) and Sales Managers $148,270 (38% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Executive roles usually need a graduate degree or long experience.

faq.q: Do logistics managers need another degree?
faq.a: Rarely. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than transportation and distribution managers already have, including all of the top 10. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 75% of workers in a close match, so your track record matters most.

faq.q: What skills should logistics managers build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are social perceptiveness, operations analysis, managing people and judgment and decision making. Instructing already rates 3.62 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so reading people and leading larger teams are the main steps up.
